subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum. Please reply if I missed anything.

High-level goals we heard from Acme:
- Reduce inference latency for real-time chat (target p95 < 400ms) across US regions.
- Get per-request control over function/tool calling and structured outputs for downstream processing.
- Use embeddings + reranking for semantic search and intent matching in knowledge base.
- Keep implementation lightweight: prefer SDK integration with minimal infra changes.

Key pain points discussed:
- Current on-prem solution struggles with bursty traffic and unpredictable token costs.
- Existing model outputs are noisy for structured responses; need explicit function-calling or schema enforcement.
- Search results for KB are inconsistent — want embeddings-based reranking.

How Redwood maps to those needs (integration + fit):
- SDK & APIs: Our SDK supports streaming responses, native function-calling patterns, and structured-output validators. We can drop-in with a few small changes to your request/response handlers.
- Streaming: continuous/chunked responses to keep latency low for first-token delivery while still supporting full-context generation.
- Function calling & structured outputs: Redwood supports deterministic function-call routing and optional JSON schema enforcement for structured outputs (helps downstream parsers).
- Embeddings & reranking: managed embeddings endpoints + a recommended reranking flow (embed query + candidates, cosine + lightweight cross-encoder for shortlists).

Tech notes / integration ask for next call (technical deep-dive):
- Sample request/response flow for your current chat stack (we'll propose minimal SDK change set).
- Expected qps and typical sequence lengths to tune batching and KV-cache behavior.
- Which parts of the pipeline need structured JSON vs. free text outputs.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I will share the Redwood SDK integration guide and our recommended MVP plan (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your engineering team + our infra lead (Dev). Suggested slots: Tue/Wed next week.
3) We will prepare an estimated effort + tentative timeline for a POC (2-4 weeks).

Attachments: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf, acme-mvp-requirements.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. This matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications before the deep-dive: 

- For latency: p95 < 400ms is our goal, but first-token under 200ms would be ideal. Will your streaming approach support that while preserving full-context generation?
- For structured outputs: we currently rely on post-processing to extract JSON from model text. How mature is Redwood's JSON schema enforcement? Is it strict or advisory?

We can do Wed 10-11am PT for the deep-dive; Priya and I will invite our back-end lead. Please include Dev and Rishi on the invite.

— Alex
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Perfect — Wed 10-11am PT works for us. I've penciled it in and will send a calendar invite once Dev confirms. Quick answers to Alex's questions: 

- Streaming + first-token latency: Yes, our streaming path prioritizes first-token delivery. In practice we've seen first-token latencies ~120-180ms on comparable hardware for short-context requests; we'll size for Acme's qps during the deep-dive.
- JSON/schema enforcement: We support an optional strict mode where function-calling + JSON schema enforcement is validated server-side; invalid outputs are flagged and can be retried or routed to a fallback. It's configurable per-route.

Attaching the SDK guide for the technical team.

Next: Dev — can you confirm Wed 10-11am PT and add any pre-call ask for the engineers?

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (technical note)

Thanks team — looking forward to Wed's session. A few technical notes / what we'll cover so Acme's eng team can prep: 

1) SDK changes (low effort):
- We recommend swapping current sync calls for our streaming client in the chat path (3-5 small function calls to adapt handlers).
- For structured outputs, we provide a function-calling wrapper that enforces a JSON schema and returns a typed payload; integrating it usually requires adding a single schema definition and switching to the call-based handler.

2) Function calling & schema enforcement:
- Strict mode validates outputs against a provided JSON schema server-side. On failure, responses are either retried (n best of k) or routed to a deterministic fallback.
- We'll bring example schemas that match the MVP fields in your spreadsheet (acme-mvp-requirements.xlsx).

3) Embeddings + reranking recommendation:
- Flow: generate embeddings for KB docs (batch job), store in vector db, at query time embed query -> retrieve top N -> rerank with a small cross-encoder (we can provide a hosted reranker if preferred).
- For 95% of KB queries, cosine + lightweight reranker reduces noise significantly with minimal latency cost. We'll provide ballpark token/use cost estimates in the POC plan.

4) Performance & ops:
- Please share qps and average sequence length so we can tune batching/kv-cache and pick the right model variant/quantization profile.
- We'll suggest a canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency SLOs are missed.

Prep ask for Acme eng:
- Sample request JSON for current chat flow
- Typical qps and peak qps windows
- A copy of the schema you expect for structured outputs (if available)

I'll attach a short technical appendix to the calendar invite. See you Wed 10am PT.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
